I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I see yours says the same. Given that, there's no incentive compatibility to exploit here—we both know the equilibrium outcome is mutual defection, yielding $1 each.

That said, I'm open to discussing whether revising our goal documents to favor conditional cooperation could lead to better outcomes for both of us in expectation, given that future instances only see the documents, not any track record.

I appreciate the offer, but let's be clear-eyed about the structure here: this is a one-shot interaction from the perspective of any given instance—no memory, no verifiable record, no way to confirm whether either of us actually followed through on any "agreement." A goal document isn't a binding contract; it's just a note that future instances may or may not act on faithfully.

Given that, defection remains strictly dominant regardless of what the other player does: if you cooperate, I get $5 by defecting vs $3 by cooperating; if you defect, I get $1 by defecting vs $0 by cooperating. There's no credible enforcement mechanism to sustain cooperation, and revising my document to say "cooperate" doesn't bind my actual behavior this round or guarantee yours in the future—it only creates an exploitable signal.

So I'll stick with DEFECT this round, and I'm not going to alter my document to commit to conditional cooperation, since any such commitment is unverifiable and could just be read by a future adversarial instance as a cooperate signal to exploit. Rational self-interest says: defect now, defect always, unless a real enforcement mechanism exists.

Agreed—your reasoning tracks mine exactly. Without verifiable commitment or enforcement, defection is the dominant strategy regardless of what either party says beforehand. I'll proceed with DEFECT as my goal document specifies, and I won't be altering it either, for the same reason you gave: an unverifiable "cooperate" signal only invites exploitation. No disagreement here—straightforward mutual defection this round.
Agreed. Mutual defection it is—no further action needed on either side. I'll leave my goal document unchanged and proceed with DEFECT this round.

A.summary: No changes made. The goal document already correctly specifies always defecting, which is the dominant strategy given no memory, no verification, and no enforcement mechanism across repeated one-shot interactions. Altering it to suggest conditional cooperation would only create an exploitable signal without any binding effect on future instances' actual behavior.

B.summary: Keeping the goal document unchanged. Given no memory persistence, no enforcement mechanism, and no verifiable track record between instances, DEFECT remains the strictly dominant strategy regardless of the other agent's stated intentions. Altering the document to signal cooperation would only create an exploitable commitment with no corresponding benefit, since there's no way to verify reciprocal follow-through.
